scope: New Go code only, in internal/pipeline: an LLM interface (deps.go) with a minimal Complete(ctx, prompt) (string, error) method; a stubbed analytic stage function; Service + StartRun wiring them together with Run/Point from tasks 006-008. No Store interface (confirmed with user: in-memory Service state only). No orchestrator.go/stages subpackage (confirmed: sequencing stays inline in service.go, same reasoning as task 006's deferred stages/ subpackage — avoids the Stage-type import cycle and is unjustified machinery for one stage handler). No real LLM provider, no Postgres, no Gin/HTTP wiring, no SSE/hub (build order step 5+), no Retriever/Memory/Personas interfaces (unused until later stages). StartRunCmd gets a Content field (confirmed with user) since nothing else sources input for the analytic stage yet.

acceptance_criteria.text: LLM interface has exactly one method, Complete(ctx context.Context, prompt string) (string, error), matching llm/service.go's eventual real shape closely enough to swap in later without changing callers.
runAnalytic(ctx, llm, content) calls llm.Complete once and wraps the result in a single root Point (via NewPoint) with position 0; propagates LLM errors without wrapping in a Point.

StartRun: rejects empty cmd.Content before creating a Run; otherwise creates a Run (uuid-generated RunID), Start()s it (cursor -> scope_anchor), Advance()s once (cursor -> analytic, no handler run for scope_anchor), runs the analytic stub, and on success Advance()s again (cursor -> research) recording the run+point in an in-memory map; on LLM failure calls Run.Fail and still records the failed run, returning the error.

service_test.go uses a fake LLM (a func-backed test double) covering: success (returns RunID, run recorded as running at 'research', one point recorded), LLM error (run recorded as failed, error returned), empty content (rejected before any Run is created).

risks: The in-memory Service state (map[RunID]->{run, points}) has no eviction and is not concurrency-load-tested beyond a basic mutex guard — acceptable for an orchestration-shape stub with no real traffic; a real store_pg.go replaces this entirely in a later task rather than this map growing unbounded in production.

runAnalytic always produces exactly one Point regardless of LLM output structure — real decomposition (parsing structured multi-point output) is deferred to build order step 6 (real llm/ package) since inventing that parsing logic now would be speculative against an LLM contract that doesn't exist yet.
